# 1. Scientific Scope and Clinical Disclaimer

`SigBenchR` is a research benchmarking framework designed to evaluate whether a transcriptomic gene signature discriminates immunotherapy response classes across multiple cohorts and whether it provides predictive value independent of baseline T-cell infiltration.

* **Research use only:** `SigBenchR` is not a calibrated clinical decision support device. ROC-AUC and PR-AUC quantify rank-based class discrimination, not patient-level response probability.
* **Subsampled packaged cohorts vs. full transcriptomes:** The bundled melanoma ICI datasets (`datasets_ici`: `van_allen_2015`, `hugo_2016`, `riaz_2017`, `gide_2019`) contain ~2,800 genes to keep package size under 5 MB. Null permutation runs on these cohorts are labeled `background_type = "subsampled_panel_cohort"`. For full-transcriptome evaluations (`universe_size >= 5000`, `background_type = "full_transcriptome"`), load complete matrices via `read_user_dataset()` or `load_cohort_bundle()`.

```{r load-pkg}
library(SigBenchR)
data(datasets_ici, package = "SigBenchR")
sigs <- get_builtin_signatures(include_controls = TRUE)
```

# 2. Cancer Immunology Signatures and Continuous Regression Weights

Built-in signatures carry 15 standardized metadata fields (`signature_name`, `biological_interpretation`, `genes`, `genes_up`, `genes_down`, `gene_directions`, `weights`, `min_genes`, `species`, `direction`, `category`, `derived_from`, `original_reference`, `doi`, `scoring_compatibility`, `known_limitations`).

* **Weighted 18-gene `T_Cell_Inflamed_GEP`:** Uses the published continuous linear regression coefficients from Ayers et al. (*JCI* 2017) and Cristescu et al. (*Science* 2018), preserving the negative coefficient on **`CD276` (B7-H3, `-0.023900`)** alongside 17 positive IFN-$\gamma$ and adaptive resistance genes (e.g., **`STAT1 = 0.250229`**, **`CMKLR1 = 0.151253`**, **`LAG3 = 0.123895`**). Note that evaluating these weights on cohort RNA-seq scales does not claim analytical equivalence to the proprietary NanoString nCounter housekeeping-normalized clinical assay.
* **Separation of biological axes:** Classic IFN-$\gamma$-induced adaptive checkpoint molecules (`Checkpoint_Axis`, 9 genes: `PDCD1`, `CD274`, `PDCD1LG2`, `CTLA4`, `LAG3`, `HAVCR2`, `TIGIT`, `IDO1`, `VSIR`) are separated from non-classical immune-exclusion B7 family members (`B7_Immune_Exclusion`, 3 genes: `CD276`, `VTCN1`, `HHLA2`, `direction = "negative"`).
* **Myeloid suppression specificity:** `Myeloid_Suppression` (`direction = "negative"`) excludes the pan-macrophage marker `CD68` and the IFN-$\gamma$-inducible gene `IDO1`.

```{r inspect-gep}
gep <- sigs[["T_Cell_Inflamed_GEP"]]
gep$weights[c("STAT1", "LAG3", "CD274", "CD276")]
```

# 3. Mouse-to-Human Ortholog Mapping & Background Preservation

When benchmarking mouse preclinical cohorts (`map_mouse_to_human()`), blind uppercase conversion and contested polymorphic MHC paralogs are disabled by default:

* `ortholog_policy = "strict_1to1"` (default) retains only unambiguous 1:1 orthologs; `"many_to_1"` collapses many-to-1 mouse paralogs using `collapse_fun`; ambiguous 1:many mouse-to-human mappings are always rejected and logged in `attr(res, "ortholog_stats")`.
* When `keep_unmapped_context = TRUE` (default), the full pre-mapping transcriptome is preserved in `attr(res, "transcriptome_bg_expr")` so single-sample rank scoring (`ss_rank`) and `null_permutation_test()` sample from the full transcriptome rather than collapsing to the mapped gene subset.

```{r ortholog-demo}
set.seed(801)
mouse_genes <- c("Ifng", "Cxcl9", "Stat1", "Cd274", "Cd8a", "Gzma", paste0("MouseBg", 1:60))
mouse_mat <- matrix(
  rnorm(length(mouse_genes) * 16, mean = 5, sd = 1.2),
  nrow = length(mouse_genes),
  dimnames = list(mouse_genes, paste0("M", 1:16))
)
mapped_mat <- map_mouse_to_human(mouse_mat, ortholog_policy = "strict_1to1", keep_unmapped_context = TRUE)
ostat <- attr(mapped_mat, "ortholog_stats")
c(n_input = ostat$n_input, n_mapped = ostat$n_mapped, context_preserved = ostat$context_preserved)
```

# 4. Null Permutation Calibration, Multiple Testing Families & PR-AUC Diagnostics

* **2D Expression-and-Dispersion Matching:** With `match_expression = TRUE`, `null_permutation_test()` bins candidate genes across a 2D grid of **5 mean-expression quantiles $\times$ 3 gene-SD tertiles** (with 1D mean-quantile fallback) and applies the observed signature's continuous weight distribution (`weights`) to each random draw.
* **Hypothesis Families (`adjust_null_p()`):** `run_benchmark()` reports raw `null_p`, within-method BH FDR (`null_p_adj_bh`), and across-method global BH FDR (`null_p_adj_bh_global`) in separate columns.
* **PR-AUC Tie and Small-Class Guards (`pr_auc()`):** Reports `tie_fraction`, `small_positive_class` ($n_{\text{pos}} < 5$ or $n_{\text{neg}} < 5$), `n_boot_valid`, and `ci_unreliable`.

```{r bench-diagnostics}
res <- suppressWarnings(run_benchmark(
  signatures = sigs[c("IFNG6", "T_Cell_Inflamed_GEP", "Cytolytic_Activity")],
  datasets = datasets_ici[c("van_allen_2015", "gide_2019")],
  methods = c("mean", "zscore"),
  compute_pr = TRUE,
  n_boot = 30L,
  compute_null = TRUE,
  n_perm = 25L,
  match_expression = TRUE,
  seed = 42L
))
res[, c(
  "dataset", "signature", "method", "auc", "pr_auc", "ci_unreliable",
  "null_p", "null_p_adj_bh", "null_p_adj_bh_global", "background_type"
)]
```

# 5. Testing Predictive Value Beyond T-Cell Infiltration

`test_beyond_infiltration()` evaluates whether a signature adds value beyond a reference infiltration axis (`response ~ sig_score_z + inf_score_z` vs `response ~ inf_score_z`):

* **Leakage-free fold-inside scaling:** Per-gene `zscore`/`rank` parameters and logistic predictor standardization are estimated strictly inside each training fold and applied to the test fold.
* **Paired fold-level CV $\Delta\text{AUC}$:** Reports `delta_auc_combined`, `sd_delta_auc`, `delta_auc_ci_low`, and `delta_auc_ci_high`.
* **Diagnostic gates & Directional Stouffer Z:** `adds_independent_value` requires BH-adjusted `lrt_p_adj_bh < 0.05`. Low Events Per Variable ($\text{EPV} < 5 \implies \text{low\_epv}$) and multicollinearity ($\text{VIF} \ge 5 \implies \text{high\_collinearity}$; $\text{VIF} \ge 10 \implies \text{failed\_collinearity}$) are flagged via `analysis_status`. Cross-cohort synthesis uses sample-size weighted **directional Stouffer Z** (`combined_lrt_p`, `stouffer_z`, `direction_conflict`) so opposite-sign cohort effects cancel rather than inflating significance.

```{r beyond-inf-demo}
bi <- test_beyond_infiltration(
  datasets = datasets_ici[c("van_allen_2015", "gide_2019")],
  signature = sigs[["IFNG6"]],
  infiltration_axis = "IFN_Gamma",
  method = "zscore",
  n_folds = 4L,
  n_repeats = 2L,
  seed = 42L
)
bi$summary[, c("infiltration_axis", "n_cohorts", "n_independent", "stouffer_z", "combined_lrt_p", "direction_conflict")]
bi$per_cohort[, c("cohort", "n", "epv", "vif", "delta_auc_combined", "lrt_p", "lrt_p_adj_bh", "analysis_status")]
```
